title: Condition and concession linkers
titleVi: Từ nối chỉ điều kiện và nhượng bộ
summary: unless, provided that, in case, even if, albeit — điều kiện và nhượng bộ ở mức C1, không dùng will sau các từ nối này.
whyItMatters: Đây là nhóm cấu trúc phân biệt band 7 với band 8 trong Task 2: **điều kiện có giới hạn** (*provided that*), **đề phòng** (*in case*), **nhượng bộ** (*albeit*, *notwithstanding*). Sai thì rất rõ: *unless you will*, *in case of you forget*, *even though* dùng cho giả định. Giám khảo coi đây là bằng chứng của *complex structures* — nhưng chỉ khi dùng đúng.

sections.heading: unless = except if, not simply if not
body: **Unless** means *except if*: *You cannot enter **unless** you are a member* (= you can enter only if you are a member). It introduces a **clause**, and like all future conditionals it takes a **present tense**, never *will*: *Unless it stops raining, we will cancel.*

Do not use *unless* as a mechanical substitute for *if … not*. When the *if*-clause describes a cause of your reaction rather than an exception, *unless* changes the meaning: *I'll be angry if you don't come* (your absence causes anger) is not *I'll be angry unless you come* (anger applies in every case except your coming).
*Unless* can be followed by a negative clause in formal writing, but the result is tricky; if in doubt, write *if … not*.

examples.right: Unless the council acts soon, the shortage will worsen.
examples.wrong: Unless the council will act soon, the shortage will worsen.

examples.right: The scheme cannot succeed unless local people are consulted.
examples.note: *except if* — the only route to success.

examples.right: I'll be disappointed if the report is not published this week.
examples.wrong: I'll be disappointed unless the report is published this week.
examples.note: The *unless* version means disappointment in every case except publication — too strong.

sections.heading: as long as, provided that, on condition that
body: These set an explicit **condition**: *You can borrow the car **as long as** you drive carefully.* *The data may be reused **provided that** the source is cited.*
**Provided (that)** and **providing (that)** are the most formal and the most common in academic writing; **as long as** is neutral; **on condition that** is legalistic and adds emphasis.
Again, no *will*: *Provided the weather is good, the event will go ahead.* The subordinate clause stays in the present even though the meaning is future.

rows: as a precaution because something might happen

sections.heading: in case vs if: precaution, not condition
body: **In case** explains why you take a precaution **now**: *Take an umbrella **in case** it rains.* You do not know whether it will rain; the umbrella is insurance.
**If** states a condition and its result: *Take an umbrella **if** it rains.* Here the umbrella is conditional on the rain.
So *in case* is followed by a present tense (never *will*), and **in case of** takes a noun: *In case of fire, use the stairs.* The two forms are not interchangeable: *in case of it rains* is wrong.

examples.right: I'll write down the password in case I forget it.
examples.wrong: I'll write down the password in case I will forget it.

examples.right: In case of emergency, call this number.
Take a map if you get lost.
examples.wrong: Take a map in case you get lost, otherwise you will be lost.
examples.note: The *if* version makes the map conditional; *in case* makes it a precaution. Both are possible, but don't mix the logic.

sections.heading: Concession: even if, even though, while, albeit
body: **Even though** concedes a **fact**: *Even though the evidence is clear, the ministry has delayed the ban.* **Even if** concedes a **hypothesis**: *Even if the evidence were clear, the ministry would delay the ban.* Mixing them misrepresents what you know.

**While** and **whilst** can concede at the start of a clause: *While the policy has merits, its costs are unevenly distributed.* **Albeit** introduces an adjective or noun phrase with no subject — a C1 marker: *a useful, **albeit** expensive, tool*.
For the most formal register, use **notwithstanding + noun** (*Notwithstanding these objections, the plan proceeded*) or **for all + noun** (*For all its faults, the system works*).

examples.right: Even if tuition were free, enrolment would still depend on transport costs.
Even though tuition is free, enrolment remains low in remote districts.
The reform, albeit controversial, has reduced waiting times.
examples.wrong: The reform, albeit it is controversial, has reduced waiting times.
examples.note: **albeit** takes a phrase, not a clause.

sections.heading: Formal condition frames for band 8
body: Academic writing often drops **if** and inverts instead. **Should + subject + verb**: *Should the government decide to intervene, the costs would fall.* **Were it not for + noun**: *Were it not for the subsidy, the industry would collapse.* **Had it not been for + noun**: *Had it not been for the grant, the project would never have started.*
These frames are marked C1 because they combine condition, inversion and a formal register. One per essay is enough; three looks like a display.

Use **otherwise** or **or else** to state the consequence of failing the condition: *The funding must be renewed; **otherwise**, the service will close.* **Otherwise** is neutral; **or else** is conversational and best avoided in Writing.

examples.right: Should the pilot succeed, the scheme will be extended nationwide.
Were it not for remittances, many rural households would fall below the poverty line.
Had it not been for the 2008 crisis, the reform might have passed.
examples.note: **Had it not been for** + past reference.

commonMistakes.wrong: Unless the government will invest more, the system will collapse.
commonMistakes.right: Unless the government invests more, the system will collapse.
commonMistakes.why: Sau **unless** (như sau *if*) không dùng *will*. Mệnh đề điều kiện dùng hiện tại đơn.

commonMistakes.wrong: In case of you forget your password, write it down.
commonMistakes.right: In case you forget your password, write it down.
commonMistakes.why: **in case of** + danh từ; **in case** + mệnh đề. Trộn hai dạng là lỗi cấu trúc.

commonMistakes.wrong: Even though the plan were perfect, it would still cost too much.
commonMistakes.right: Even if the plan were perfect, it would still cost too much.
commonMistakes.why: Giả định không có thật dùng **even if** + giả định cách; **even though** dành cho sự thật đã biết.

commonMistakes.wrong: The reform, albeit it is controversial, has reduced waiting times.
commonMistakes.right: The reform, albeit controversial, has reduced waiting times.
commonMistakes.why: **albeit** đứng trước cụm tính từ/danh từ, không đứng trước mệnh đề.

commonMistakes.wrong: Provided that the weather will be good, the event will go ahead.
commonMistakes.right: Provided that the weather is good, the event will go ahead.
commonMistakes.why: Các từ nối điều kiện (**provided, as long as, unless, in case**) không nhận *will* trong mệnh đề phụ.

ieltsTips: Dùng **provided that** để nêu điều kiện của một giải pháp trong đoạn problem–solution: *Charging for plastic bags is effective, **provided that** alternatives are affordable.* Câu này thể hiện tư duy phản biện, không chỉ liệt kê giải pháp.

Dùng **in case** để giải thích chính sách phòng ngừa: *Governments should fund reserves **in case** supply chains are disrupted.* Khác hoàn toàn với *if*, và chính sự khác biệt này là thứ giám khảo ghi nhận.
Dùng **even if** để nhượng bộ một giả định rồi phản bác: ***Even if** remote work reduced commuting, it would not solve the housing crisis.* Đây là cấu trúc của một lập luận band 8.

Dùng **Should + subject + verb** một lần trong bài để tạo giọng trang trọng: ***Should** the trend continue, demand will outstrip supply by 2030.* Đừng dùng quá một lần — hiệu quả sẽ giảm và câu dễ sai trật tự từ.

exercises.question: ___ the council acts soon, the shortage will worsen.
You can borrow the car ___ you drive carefully.
exercises.explanation: A condition the borrower must meet → **as long as**.

exercises.question: Take an umbrella ___ it rains.
exercises.explanation: A precaution + clause → **in case**. *In case of* needs a noun.

exercises.question: ___ the evidence were clear, the ministry would still delay the ban.
___ the pilot succeed, the scheme will be extended.
The data may be reused ___ that the source is cited.
___ case the system fails, keep a paper copy.
The reform, ___ controversial, has reduced waiting times.
___ it not been for the grant, the project would never have started.
The funding must be renewed; ___ , the service will close.
exercises.explanation: **otherwise** states what happens if the condition fails.
